Questions.question: Why does the instructor check the machine guard alignment first?
Questions.answer: Because the guard protects the operator.
options: Because the operator protects the guard.
Because the guard protects the operator.
Because the guard protects the machine.

Questions.question: Why does the instructor switch off the main power supply before loosening the chuck?
Questions.answer: To ensure the machine is completely safe to work on.
options: To ensure the tool is easier to remove.
To ensure the machine is completely safe to work on.
To ensure the machine is working.

Questions.question: Why is the chuck loosened using the key carefully?
Questions.answer: To avoid sudden movement of parts.
options: To avoid sudden loss of parts.
To avoid sudden movement of parts.
To avoid losing the key.

Questions.question: Why is the machine run at low speed after fitting the new tool?
Questions.answer: To check for vibration or unusual noise.
options: To check for vibration and noise.
To check for vibration or unusual noise.
To check for unusual noise and speed.

Questions.question: Why does the instructor stress the order of the safety inspection steps?
Questions.answer: Because missing steps can cause safety problems later.
options: Because missing steps can cause safety inspections later.
Because missing steps can cause safety problems later.
Because missing problems can cause issues later.

activity_c.text: Good morning, everyone.
Let’s get started.
Today, I want to explain two routine processes that we practise in the Mechanical Technology section.
First, I will explain a basic cutting tool change on a lathe machine.
After that, we will move on to a simple machine safety inspection.
Please listen carefully and follow the steps in the correct order.
First, let’s look at the cutting tool change process.
In our workshop, this task is usually done before a machining job begins.
Before touching the machine, we check the machine guard alignment.
The guard must be in the correct position to protect the operator.
Next, we switch off the main power supply.
This step is very important, and we never skip it, even if the machine is not running.
After that, we loosen the chuck using the key.
We do this slowly and carefully to avoid sudden movement.
Once the chuck is loose, we remove the worn cutting tool from the tool holder.
A worn tool affects surface finish and accuracy.
Then, we fit the new cutting tool securely in the correct position.
We make sure it is tight and properly aligned.
Finally, we run the machine at low speed.
This allows us to check for vibration or unusual noise before starting full operation.
If everything looks normal, the tool change is complete.
Now, let’s move on to the machine safety inspection process.
This inspection is usually done at the start of the day.
First, we visually inspect the machine body and controls.
Next, we check that emergency stop buttons are working correctly.
After that, we look for oil leaks or loose parts around the machine.
Finally, we clean the work area and remove unnecessary tools.
We always follow this order, because safety checks reduce accidents and machine damage.
Missing a step can cause serious problems later.
